metadata.title: The impact of reading metacognitive strategies on mathematics learning efficiency and performance: An analysis using PISA 2018 data in China

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata for 15-year-old students from four Chinese provinces, with an analytic sample of 11,993 after removing 65 cases with missing data for key variables. The manuscript does not report the use of PISA sampling weights or any replicate-weight scheme, nor does it name any weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or describe complex-survey variance estimation. Because the analyses are person-centered (latent profile analysis) and regression-based (logistic and linear regressions), the paper does not document whether estimates were population-representative for the target provinces. As a result, readers should treat the reported associations as conditional on the analyzed sample and consider re-running with PISA-provided weights if available for inference to the underlying population.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2018 data for 15-year-old students sampled from 361 schools across four Chinese provinces. The authors removed 65 cases with missing data (0.53%) due to lack of data for key variables, yielding a final analytic sample of 11,993 students (5743 females, 6250 males).

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Reading (15-year-olds, China; metacognitive strategy dimensions UNDREM/METASUM/METASPAM)
main_findings.target_variable: Reading metacognitive strategy profile membership (6 latent profiles)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Latent profile analysis fit: selected 6 profiles (Entropy 0.871; AIC/BIC/aBIC lowest among candidates; LMR and BLRT p-values significant). Profile sizes: 6.0%, 18.2%, 9.0%, 38.3%, 20.0%, 8.5%. Logistic regression results reported as odds ratios (OR) with 95% CIs in Table 4.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading the study leveraged Gender, Economic, social, cultural status, and School location (rural/city) to predict reading metacognitive strategy profile membership, finding that the distribution of profiles was primarily influenced by Gender and ESCS (with school location having a smaller impact). This indicates that improving reading metacognitive strategy instruction may need to be differentiated by students’ gender and socioeconomic background to reduce stratification in strategy use, though the cross-sectional design limits causal claims.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Mathematics (15-year-olds, China; PV1MATH–PV10MATH averaged to MATHACH)
main_findings.target_variable: Mathematics performance (MATHACH) within each reading-strategy profile
main_findings.performance_metrics: Multiple linear regression within profiles: overall weekly learning time effect β = 0.034, p < 0.001. Profile-specific effects: Novice-indifferent β = 0.158, p < 0.001; Veteran-average β = 0.057, p < 0.01; Novice-low evaluating β = 0.064, p < 0.05; Novice-arbitrary β = 0.079, p < 0.01; Veteran-skilled β = −0.015, p = 0.298; Novice-mixed β = 0.025, p = 0.202.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Mathematics the study leveraged Weekly math learning time (and profile membership defined from reading metacognitive dimensions) to predict mathematics performance, finding that learning time positively predicted performance for four profiles but showed no significant effect for Veteran-skilled and Novice-mixed, and a non-significant negative coefficient for Veteran-skilled. This indicates that policies aiming to reduce academic burden by cutting learning time should be personalized: students with weak reading metacognitive strategies may require more time or targeted strategy support, while high-performing strategy profiles may not benefit from additional time.

data.outcome_summary: This study analyzes PISA 2018 microdata from 361 schools in four Chinese provinces, focusing on 15-year-old students (final analytic sample N=11,993 after removing 65 cases with missing key variables). Reading metacognitive strategies were measured using 16 PISA items across three dimensions (Understanding & remembering, Summarizing, Assessing credibility), summarized as UNDREM, METASUM, and METASPAM, and students were grouped into six latent profiles via latent profile analysis. Mathematics performance was derived from PV1MATH–PV10MATH by averaging the ten plausible values (MATHACH), and weekly mathematics learning time (MMINS) was used to examine learning efficiency within each profile. The study reports that Gender and ESCS primarily shape profile membership, and that weekly learning time significantly predicts mathematics performance for Novice-indifferent, Veteran-average, Novice-low evaluating, and Novice-arbitrary profiles, but not for Veteran-skilled and Novice-mixed. Limitations include cross-sectional design (no causal inference) and lack of reported PISA sampling-weight usage and PV/missing-data transparency beyond the stated case deletion.
data.null_fields_interpretation: Although the paper uses person-centered modeling (latent profile analysis) and regression models, it does not train or compare machine-learning predictive algorithms (e.g., Random Forest/XGBoost/SVM). Consequently, the ML technique fields are left empty rather than forcing an ML label onto LPA/regression. The extraction therefore treats the study as exploratory rather than predictive/causal ML.
